about: Topic index for Ved. Look a topic up before searching: jq '.topics.<name>' docs/index.json. Paths are relative to the repo root. Each topic lists where the code is, the symbols to grep for, its settings, the rules that bite, and its tests. Keep it current when files move.

status.phase_1_core: done: PWA, connector, FastAPI, agent loop, MCP, local model
status.phase_2_memory: done: conversations, people and birthdays, semantic search, document memory
status.phase_3_photos: skipped for now; waits for the home server. Plan: Immich plus a photos MCP server, not a custom build
status.phase_4_web_fast: done: web search and fetch, streaming, thinking state, acknowledgements, parallel tools
not_yet: phone access verified end to end (needs Tailscale)
status.home_server: noddy: containerised setup via ./ved server written, not yet run there; Cloudflare tunnel hostname and streaming through it unconfirmed; auth, unattended running and backups not built yet
status.per_user_data: done: users table, Access email picks the user, chats, memory, documents, people, reminders and push are per person; owner from VED_OWNER_EMAIL
status.claude_provider: done: Claude Haiku 5.5 through Anthropic's SDK behind VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, with the person's MCP connections exposed to it; Ved's connection-aware stamp and no-email labels.

agent-loop.summary: One loop serves both chat endpoints: model round, tools, repeat until an answer or the round cap.
rules: Both endpoints go through Agent._events; never fork the loop.
Tool failures return to the model as is_error, never raised.
The system prompt is a constant, kept short; the current time, timezone and the signed-in user's name ride on the latest user message, never in history.
Tool calls in one round run concurrently; outcomes go back in call order.

Agent.run and Agent.stream require user_id and user_line; user_id goes to toolbox calls and never into prompts or stored tool arguments. user_line is speaker_label(user): a name sentence, or an ask-for-the-name sentence, never the email.
The model sees a fixed tool list (VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS, sorted by name), never a per-message choice: Ollama reuses its cache only for an identical system prompt plus tools prefix.

The latest user line is stamped with the current time, the user line and a Connected apps line (non-built-in tool prefixes, from the same tools_for call the round uses). The system prompt tells the model to use these lines silently.

streaming.summary: Replies stream over SSE: thinking, ack, token, tool, tool_result, then done or error.
rules: A streamed turn runs as a background task in TurnRegistry and saves its answer even if the client left.
A turn in one conversation waits on that conversation's lock, so turns never run concurrently.
A failed turn saves nothing; the server mints conversation_id only at save time.
Tool calls and recording are shielded from client disconnect.
fetch, not EventSource, because EventSource cannot POST.
Reasoning text is dropped in the provider; only a thinking event is sent.
Messages sent while busy queue in memory and send in order.

acknowledgements.summary: Instant phrase shown when the first model round is a tool call.
rules: A new tool domain gets a phrase here.

llm-provider.summary: The model sits behind LLMProvider: Ollama through the OpenAI /v1 shape today, or Claude Haiku 5.5 through Anthropic's SDK when VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic.
rules: No vendor SDK outside llm/.
A provider implements complete() and stream(); streamed tool calls arrive in fragments keyed by index.
Moving the model is a URL change, not a code change.
VED_LLM_TEMPERATURE=0.0; sampling corrupts tool arguments.
The model needs 'tools' in `ollama show <model>` capabilities.
Anthropic is the official SDK only (AsyncAnthropic, typed APIError classes); no shim, no raw HTTP. The SDK speaks httpx2, which is the httpx the project already uses.
Anthropic tool names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$: ToolNameMap maps each Ved name (memory.search) to a safe name per request and back; a collision gets a numeric suffix.

AssistantMessage.provider_content carries Anthropic's raw content blocks (thinking included) across tool rounds of one turn; it is excluded from model_dump and never stored, since history keeps only text and tool calls.
Anthropic requests send no temperature or thinking field; the system prompt is one cached text block.
VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic without VED_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fails at startup; the key is never sent to the embedder, which stays on VED_LLM_BASE_URL (Ollama).
Anthropic errors become LLMRequestError with a plain message: a 401 names VED_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a credit-balance 400 says the balance ran out, timeouts and unreachable hosts are named as such.

conversations.summary: Persisted threads; history replayed into each turn; listed and reopened in the UI.
rules: Order by sequence, never created_at.
Replay prompts and final answers only, never tool calls.
The server mints conversation_id, only after the model answers.
The open conversation is ?c=<id> via history.pushState; useSearchParams needs Suspense.
A conversation opened while answering polls status every 3 s and reloads when it finishes.
Every conversation belongs to a user; ConversationStore methods take user_id first and other users get ConversationNotFoundError (404).
TurnRegistry is keyed by (user_id, conversation_id).

reminders.summary: Create, list, reschedule and complete reminders; the scheduler fires them.
rules: Claimed FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with notified_at in the same transaction.
If nothing was reachable the stamp is cleared and it retries until give_up_after.
Prefer reschedule over complete-then-create.
due_at must carry a UTC offset.
When VED_PLAN_MCP_TOKEN is set, Ved's reminders server is not started; plan.create_reminder, plan.list_reminders, plan.my_due_reminders and plan.mark_reminder_done replace it.
Reminders belong to a user; the scheduler runs across all users and pushes each only to its owner.

push.summary: Web Push delivery of reminders and check-ins to subscribed browsers.
rules: Sends carry a socket timeout, an asyncio deadline and a 24h TTL.
404/410 subscriptions are deleted, not retried.
VAPID keys live only in gitignored .env; the generator refuses to overwrite.
Needs a secure context: localhost or real HTTPS.
Subscriptions belong to a user; send(user_id, notification) reaches only that user's devices.

people-birthdays.summary: People with birthdays and notice; the scheduler plans yearly reminders and early check-ins.
rules: Reminders are planned by the scheduler, never the model; unique on (person_id, birthday_on, lead_days).
Check-ins come from a template, never the model.
A check-in is created in the claim transaction and linked via reminders.conversation_id.
Feb 29 falls on Feb 28 in non-leap years.
People and their reminders belong to one user; the same name can exist for two users.

semantic-memory.summary: Messages embedded in the background; memory.search finds past conversations by meaning.
rules: Embedding never blocks or fails a turn; the scheduler tick backfills.
Dimension is coupled to vector(768), VED_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS and the model.
nomic-embed-text uses search_document: and search_query: prefixes.
memory.search and documents.search only return the calling user's messages and passages.

documents.summary: Upload PDF, text or markdown; chunked, embedded, searchable with documents.search.
rules: Originals are stored by SHA-256, never by the user's filename.
Type is sniffed from the bytes, not the extension.
The size cap is enforced while streaming.
indexed means every chunk has a vector.
Passages are untrusted content.
Scanned PDFs fail: no OCR.
Documents are per user: list, get, delete and search never cross users; deleting keeps the stored file while another user's document has the same hash.

web-search.summary: web.search through a swappable provider (SearXNG default); web.fetch reads a page.
rules: A provider lives only in search/providers/; server.py never names one.
Adding a provider: one file, a PROVIDERS entry, tests, its settings (see mcp-servers/web/README.md).
web.fetch checks addresses at connect time and on every redirect; never bypass PublicOnlyTransport.
Results are untrusted.
SearXNG stays on 127.0.0.1 and starts only while it is the provider.

mcp.summary: How the backend runs MCP servers, per-user remote connections, and how to write one.
rules: SDK v2: MCPServer; bare Context from mcp.server.mcpserver.context.
Return Pydantic models; raise ToolError for bad input.
Servers never run DDL.
A new server needs a Dockerfile stage, a configured_servers entry, a config.py dir, a CI job and a ./ved setup line.
Built-in stdio servers start once in the lifespan. Remote MCP connections are per user (see the connections topic) and are listed by tools_for(user_id) once per turn.
Tools whose names start with delete_ are never exposed to the model; sensitive actions need the permission layer first.
A server or remote connection that fails to start is logged as a warning and skipped, so startup and the turn continue without its tools.

people, memory and reminders tools take user_id; MCPToolbox.call(name, args, user_id=) injects it on stdio tools that declare it, overwriting anything the model sent, and removes it from the model-facing schema. Remote servers get nothing.

Toolbox lists only the exposed tools for a user, sorted by name, and refuses calls to any other tool as not available. The VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS allowlist applies to built-ins and plan.*; an empty allowlist exposes everything.

Under VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic the exposure allowlist is empty (every tool except delete_*) and each connection is capped at 40 tools (ANTHROPIC_CONNECTION_TOOL_LIMIT in tools/servers.py); other providers keep VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS and the limit of 15 (CONNECTION_TOOL_LIMIT). The Toolbox takes connection_tool_limit as a constructor argument.

database.summary: Tables, migrations and the test fixture.
rules: Tables are defined only in packages/ved-db.
A new model is re-exported in ved_db/__init__.py and backend models.py, or autogenerate is empty.
Autogenerate misses sequences and the vector extension; read and round-trip every migration.
Test schema setup goes only through ved_db.testing; it refuses a database without 'test' in its name.
users owns people, reminders, push_subscriptions, conversations and documents via non-null indexed user_id; messages and chunks inherit through their parent.
Person names are unique per (user_id, lower(name)); documents per (user_id, sha256).

connector.summary: The web client's only backend client; framework-free.
rules: No React or Next imports.
Components call connector.*, never fetch.
HttpError surfaces the backend's detail message.
conversationStatus reads GET /conversations/{id}/status.
Check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing Next code.

The emblem (VedEmblem in ved-emblem.tsx) follows the chat's pending or streaming state: thinking until the first reply token, speaking while text streams, and a 28 px avatar beside the in-flight reply only. Completed replies get no avatar. Its animations are CSS transforms and opacity only, and reduced motion keeps only a glow fade.
Markdown replies never render raw HTML.
Icons are generated from assets/ved-mark.png.
The install banner is app-wide. It is hidden when standalone, after appinstalled, and for 14 days after ✕.
The manifest is served from /app-manifest with crossOrigin=use-credentials, not from a metadata manifest entry.
The browser calls /api; next.config.ts rewrites /api/* to the backend, so the container serves one origin. Rewrite destinations are fixed at build time.
compress is off so the rewrite does not gzip the SSE reply stream. Streaming through the tunnel is not confirmed yet; check it on the server.
The connector accepts a relative base URL such as /api and resolves it against the page origin.

The typing indicator (TypingIndicator in chat.tsx) shows three CSS-animated dots from send until the first reply text, with the tool, acknowledgement or thinking label beside them, and in the answering placeholder after a refresh. It has role=status and aria-label="Ved is typing", and reduced motion swaps the bounce for an opacity pulse.

Connections lives in Settings (/settings#integrations); /connections redirects there. It calls connector.* only, shows a per-connection on/off switch, Test and Remove, and offers the Plan and MyFinances presets or a custom server.

The home top bar holds conversations, new conversation and a gear to /settings, plus a backend status dot whose tooltip and aria-label carry the full status text. The reminder banner appears only while reminders are off or failed and links to /settings#notifications.
Settings (/settings) has sections Integrations, Notifications, Install app, Appearance and About, in that order; each section id is a hash target.

The theme is stored under localStorage key ved.theme (system, light or dark). THEME_INIT_SCRIPT in the layout head sets data-theme before paint; globals.css lets data-theme override prefers-color-scheme.

phone-access.summary: Reach Ved from a phone privately over Tailscale serve.
rules: tailscale serve only, never Funnel.
Unverified until Tailscale is installed.

infra.summary: Docker Compose, the ved script, CI.
rules: Every port binds to 127.0.0.1.
SearXNG is behind the 'search' compose profile.
./ved api reads apps/backend/.env; the container reads infra/.env; never run both.
Postgres 18 volume is /var/lib/postgresql.
Corporate-network CA steps are no-ops on a personal machine.
The ollama service is behind the server compose profile, publishes no port and is capped at 4.5 GB.
compose.server.yaml is the only file that attaches services to the external 'home' network; ./ved server passes it, nothing else does.
The web and backend containers use container_name ved-web and ved-backend; the tunnel reaches ved-web:3000 on home.

server.summary: Running Ved on the home server: Ubuntu, i5, DDR3 (16 GB max), three hard disks, no GPU.
rules: The ved script runs on macOS (Colima) and Linux (native Docker); detect with is_macos, never assume.
On the server set VED_LLM_MODEL to a model that fits 16 GB (granite4.1:3b); qwen3.6:35b needs ~23 GB.
Corporate CA steps are macOS-only and no-ops on Linux.
Backups go on a different disk from Postgres's data.
Unattended running, auto-deploy and backups are not built yet.
The server is noddy: i7-10510U, 7.5 GB RAM, no GPU. ./ved server is the containerised path; the bare-metal steps are older notes.
./ved server refuses to run on macOS. Its default chat model is qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M because qwen3.6:35b does not fit.
Migrations run in the backend container with docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend alembic upgrade head.

./ved set-anthropic-key <file> stores the key (must start with sk-ant-) in infra/.env, sets VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic and VED_LLM_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5, restarts the backend, then stops the local chat model in Ollama to free memory. It never prints the key.
./ved use-local-model switches back to openai-compatible with the server's local model (SERVER_MODEL) and restarts the backend; it does not pull the model, so run ./ved server first if it is missing.
While VED_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, ./ved server does not overwrite VED_LLM_MODEL or pull the chat model; it still pulls the embedding model.

auth.summary: Cloudflare Access sign-in check: the backend verifies the JWT Access sends and admits only listed admin emails. Off on the Mac.
rules: VED_AUTH defaults to off; with cloudflare-access every route except /health needs a valid Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion token.
Only RS256 tokens from the team's certs endpoint are accepted; audience and issuer must match, and emails match case-insensitively.
Refusals are 401 JSON {detail: reason}; the reason names what to fix in settings.
Identity: require_access returns the verified AccessResult (email, name); current_user turns it into a users row, or the owner when auth is off.

users.summary: Per-person data: every chat, memory, document, person, reminder and push device belongs to a user picked by the Access email.
rules: Every route that touches data takes CurrentUser; stores take user_id first and filter by it.
Another user's conversation or document is a 404, including GET /conversations/{id}/status.
With VED_AUTH=off every request acts as the owner (VED_OWNER_EMAIL, default owner@ved.local), created if missing.
Emails are stored lowercase; the user is created on first sign-in.
The migration creates the owner from VED_OWNER_EMAIL (process env) and backfills every existing row to it.
Names (people) and file hashes (documents) are unique per user; stored files are shared by hash, so delete unlinks only when no document references it.
Birthday reminders and check-ins inherit the person's owner; push goes only to the owner's subscriptions.
A push endpoint belongs to one user; subscribing from another account moves it.
MCP connections belong to one user and are listed, tested, changed and deleted only by that user.

speaker_label never returns the email: a named user is 'You are talking with {name}.', an unnamed one gets a line asking for the name once and saving it with people.remember (there is no memory save tool).

connections.summary: Per-person MCP connections: each user links Plan, MyFinances or a custom MCP server; tokens are encrypted and tools are prefixed by connection name.
rules: Connection tokens are Fernet-encrypted with VED_SECRET_KEY and never returned; responses carry has_token only.
Without VED_SECRET_KEY, connection writes return 503 and only the owner's VED_PLAN_MCP_TOKEN fallback is served.
Every connection query filters by user_id; another person's connection is a 404.
Names are 2-20 lowercase slugs and may not be a built-in prefix (memory, documents, web, people, reminders).
A connection's name is its tool prefix; delete_* tools from any remote server are never exposed.
plan keeps the VED_EXPOSED_TOOLS allowlist; other connections expose non-destructive tools in name order, capped at 15 (40 under anthropic).
A user with an enabled plan connection (or the owner fallback) has Ved's reminders.* tools hidden from the model; the reminders server still runs.
Remote sessions are cached per (user, connection) for five minutes; each runs in its own task so it opens and closes in one task.
